requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:69-79 builds the body, skips the mention entirely when `$mention === ''` and otherwise emits `mb_substr($body, 0, self::MaxContentLength - mb_strlen($mention)).$mention`, so the whole content stays at 1800 chars and the mention survives truncation; :87-95 returns `"\n<@{$id}>"` on its own line; :99-115 validates with `'/\A[0-9]{17,20}\z/'` after trim and accepts ints; config/services.php:40 and .env.example:78-79 add `DISCORD_MENTION_ID`; docs/ops/devops.md:61,70 and docs/ops/logging.md:83 document it. The unchanged no-mention branch preserves the old behaviour.

conventions.evidence: New Pest tests ship with the code (tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:125-229), docs are kept in sync in the same change (.env.example:78-79, docs/ops/devops.md:61-74, docs/ops/logging.md:83, CHANGELOG.md:24), the helper has a PHPDoc block (app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:82-86), and the code matches the existing `mb_substr`/config style of the class.

security.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:111 uses a strict ASCII allow-list `'/\A[0-9]{17,20}\z/'` after `trim`, so `@everyone`, embedded newlines and extra characters can never become a mention; the value is only interpolated as digits, and no webhook URL/secrets handling or logging was touched.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:125-161 valid mention appended on its own line; :163-173 null/empty/whitespace produce no `<@`; :175-197 invalid dataset (`@everyone`, `@here`, `abc`, 16/21 digits, newline payloads, already-wrapped id); :199-212 trim + integer acceptance; :214-229 long alert is exactly 1800 chars and still ends with the mention.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the existing `formatContent()` builder and `self::MaxContentLength` (app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:69-79); adds only two small private helpers, no new dependency, service, or config layer.

readability.evidence: Method names `mentionSuffix()`/`mentionId()` and the docblock explain the intent and the `@everyone` risk (app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:82-95); the early return keeps `formatContent()` short and matches the surrounding style.

scope.evidence: Only the alert formatter, the `services.discord` config, `.env.example`, the two required ops docs, CHANGELOG and the Discord test file changed; no unrelated refactors.

review.summary: The change adds an optional, strictly validated `DISCORD_MENTION_ID` that appends `<@id>` on its own line to every Discord ops alert, reserving room for it within the 1800-character cap while leaving the no-mention path unchanged. Config, .env.example, both ops docs, the changelog and Pest tests covering valid, empty, malformed, whitespace/integer and truncation cases are all included. The implementation is small, matches existing style, and has no security or scope problems, so I would approve it as is.
